candidates.term: The Twin inside the Hour Gate
candidates.defline: The Twin lives inside your Hour Gate: your later years rest on a few people who treat you as their equal.
candidates.reading: In later life you keep company only where you are met level, with old friends who became family and with children or younger relatives or someone you train who speak to you as equals. Because dignity matters more to you than comfort, you turn down help that comes with pity. You keep learning through the few people who still argue with you. The circle gets smaller as the decades pass, and you lean on the ones who remain more than you admit.
candidates.teaser: Your later years run on a few chosen equals, friends who became family. Invest in that small circle now: it is the pension no market touches.

domain_readings.Family: Your late family is chosen as much as given: friends who became kin, children raised to stand level, a table where respect outranks ceremony. The root wants peers, so become one to your own descendants. The household that debates you as an equal is the one that keeps you young.
domain_readings.Growth: Growth in the last era comes through the small circle: two or three equals who never needed you weak, sharpening you to the end. Invest in those bonds now like the pension they are. Solitary strength ages fine. Companioned strength ages well.

candidates.life_chapter: Your late chapter roots in chosen company: the harvest decades run on a few level bonds, tended long, trusted completely. Expect the final era to be sturdier than most people’s and smaller than most people’s, by design. The circle you build by fifty is the one that carries you after.
candidates.relations: The chosen equals are this seat’s people: old friends with keys to your house, children who grew into peers, the late companions who knock without ceremony. Keep them close and keep them few. This root holds by depth, never by width.
candidates.turn_catalyst: Run thin, the circle thins with it: harvest years spent respected and unaccompanied. Recruit one equal this year. It is not too late, and never was.
candidates.turn_friction: Run heavy, the small circle seals: newcomers vetted into oblivion. Leave one chair deliberately empty and see who sits.
candidates.shadow_line: Overloaded, chosen few becomes chosen none: dignity kept, company lost.
candidates.health_line: Late health tracks companionship here: the tended body follows the tended bond. Walk with someone, and both outlast the actuary.

Family.headline: Your family in later life is chosen as much as born.
Family.recognition: You treat the younger people in your family as equals, and you want their argument more than their care. Because being looked down on is the one thing you cannot bear, you hide a hard week from anyone young enough to fuss. Your family stays close in a level way, and you miss some of the softness it rarely offers.
Family.lived: Your family has come to include people you chose since your late forties, old friends with a key and younger people who treat you as their match. You have kept that circle small on purpose, and you have seen less of the relatives who fussed over you.
Family.ahead: From your late forties the people after you grow into equals who stand beside you and argue back. You keep a smaller family around you in these years than most people do, and you are prouder of it than of anything you own.

Growth.headline: You keep growing through the few who match you.
Growth.recognition: You grow in later life through two or three people who push you as hard as you push yourself. Because you learn only from someone you respect, you ignore advice from anyone who talks down to you. Your progress is slower without that small company, and you notice it within weeks.
Growth.lived: A few equals have taught you most since your late forties, a friend or a colleague who would not let you coast. Whenever you worked alone for long your progress stalled, and you went back to them each time.
Growth.ahead: Your growth from your late forties comes through company, long talks and shared work with people who expect a great deal of you. You stay sharper in these years than most people your age, and you owe it to the few who keep you honest.
